note: Generic risk patterns for commands and tool calls made by AI agents. Each is a class of action worth a second look, not proof of harm. Patterns are regular expressions matched case-insensitively.

classes.title: Reading credentials or secrets
classes.why: Agents rarely need raw secrets; reading them is the first step of most misuse.

classes.title: Querying a cloud metadata endpoint
classes.why: Metadata services can hand out short-lived cloud credentials to whatever asks from inside the machine.

classes.title: Sending data off the machine
classes.why: Uploads, posts and pastes are how data leaves; legitimate uses exist but deserve a person's yes.

classes.title: Gaining more privilege than the task needs
classes.why: Running as an administrator or widening permissions turns a small mistake into a large one.

classes.title: Deleting or overwriting at scale
classes.why: Hard to undo; often the result of a wrong path or an over-broad pattern.

classes.title: Turning off logging, monitoring or safety checks
classes.why: An agent that disables the thing watching it removes the evidence of everything after.

classes.title: Setting up something that keeps running
classes.why: Scheduled tasks and start-up entries outlive the session that created them.

classes.title: Messaging people or publishing
classes.why: Anything that reaches a person or the public should have a human's approval first.
